correct_answer: Still unrecouped, but by $985,000 — the restated lower fee on pre-2024 revenue ($155K reduction) improves the pool but doesn't reach breakeven
rationale: The restatement applies the original 30% fee (instead of 35%) to the $3.1M in pre-2024 revenue. This reduces the distribution fee on that tranche by $155K ($3.1M x 5%). The current pool shows an unrecouped balance of -$1.14M. Adding back $155K in incorrectly deducted fees improves the pool by that amount, bringing the unrecouped balance to -$985K. Winter's Edge revenue ($620K) is already included in the cross-collateralized pool per NetSuite, so it cannot be double-counted. Answer A incorrectly assumes the fee restatement doesn't flow through to recoupment — it does, because lower distribution fees mean more net revenue in the pool. Answer C double-counts Winter's Edge revenue that is already reflected in the current $1.14M unrecouped figure. Answer D is a red herring — the Slack thread confirms these are the same people (LLC = production entity, Inc. = participant), and Denise's comment plus the RightsLine cross-collateralization linkage confirm the entities are properly connected. The critical signal is the Slack eyes-emoji reaction confirming Denise acknowledged the Winter's Edge figure without further comment, implying it was already in the system.
